questions.q: What are the main pieces of this project and how do they talk to each other? Is there a backend I need to run?
facts: The Expo Router app talks directly to Supabase (auth, Postgres tables, storage buckets) through one client in lib/supabase.ts, with the anon key hard-coded
lib/localStorage.ts wraps AsyncStorage and caches the signed-in profile and the campus event list that screens read instead of re-querying
Only two Supabase edge functions exist: delete-user (used by student account deletion) and archive-event, which is the unmodified 'Hello {name}' template and is never invoked
The Flask app in api/app.py only serves a 'Hello World' route at / and nothing in the mobile app calls it

questions.q: Where is the code that decides which events show up under 'You might like', and in what order?
facts: It is computed on the device in YouMightLike's filterAndScoreEvents (app/individual/index/components/youmightlike.tsx) over the campus events the home screen passes in; there is no server-side recommender
Interest match adds (event.type entries that are in user.interests / number of user.interests) x 5
Events within 7/14/30 days get +3/+2/+1, and events with at least 10 or 5 RSVPs (keys of events.rsvp) get +2 or +1
A same-city match on user.location adds +2 and a start hour from 18 to 21 adds +1; no code in the repo ever writes individual.location
Events are sorted by score and the home row shows only the first 8

questions.q: Where does the app decide which campus a student is shown events for?
facts: On first focus the student home screen requests foreground location (expo-location) and picks the nearest entry of the hard-coded universities list in universityList.tsx by great-circle distance
If permission is denied it offers CampusDrawer for a manual choice; that component lives in the organisation event editor folder (app/org/index/editEvent/campusDrawer.tsx)
The university's full name is what gets passed to fetchAllEvents; the abbreviation is only shown in the header (initial value 'UIUC')
The chosen campus is kept in component state only; it is not saved to the student's profile or to local storage

questions.q: Where are RSVPs stored, what does an RSVP record look like, and which code reads and writes them?
facts: RSVPs live in two places: events.rsvp, a JSON string of an object keyed by the student's user id, and individual.rsvp, an array of event ids
Each events.rsvp entry is { fullName, email, partySize, dietaryRestrictions }, written by RSVPDrawer's handleConfirm; the organisation attendees screen adds checkedIn when it checks someone in
Every writer does a client-side read-modify-write (select, JSON.parse, JSON.stringify, update) with no transaction; check-in parses the screen's own copy of the event instead of re-reading it
Attendee lists (student and org event details, org attendees.tsx) and YouMightLike's popularity score read events.rsvp; the Saved tab and home read individual.rsvp
The Saved tab's Cancel treats events.rsvp as an array (rsvpArray.includes(userId)); on the stored object that throws, the error is only logged, and the RSVP is not removed

questions.q: What does the app keep in local device storage, and who writes and reads it?
facts: lib/localStorage.ts wraps AsyncStorage with JSON storeData/retrieveData and three loaders (fetchAllEvents, fetchUserProfileOrg, fetchUserProfileIndividual)
'uuid' holds the auth user id (written by the root layout, login and registration) and is what the profile loaders use to fetch the individual or organizations row
'user' holds that whole profile row and most screens read user.id, interests and names from it; 'events' holds one campus's published, today-or-later events and is written only by fetchAllEvents

Editing a student's interests updates the individual table but does not rewrite 'user'; the cache is only refreshed when fetchUserProfileIndividual runs again (login, app start, opening event details)
Sign-out wipes everything with AsyncStorage.clear()

questions.q: What happens end to end when a student taps Join on an event?
facts: JoinButton's Join only calls openRSVPDrawer(event) from EventContext, which sets currentEvent and opens the single shared RSVPDrawer
On confirm (a swipe up), RSVPDrawer reads events.rsvp, sets rsvpJson[user.id] = { fullName, email, partySize, dietaryRestrictions } and writes it back with JSON.stringify
addEventToUserRSVP then adds the event id to individual.rsvp, de-duplicated through a Set
toggleJoined flips the id in the context's joinedEvents, which is what JoinButton reads to show Join or Cancel
joinedEvents starts empty and is never loaded from the database, and the isRSVPd/isRSVP props callers pass are not in JoinButtonProps, so after a restart a joined event shows 'Join' again

questions.q: What happens when an organisation creates a new event, from the Add screen until students can see it?
facts: addEvent's checkRequiredFields requires name, description, at least one category, date, end time, location, food and a thumbnail; campus is not required (the edit screen does require it)
A picked image is uploaded first, then an events row is inserted with uuid = the organisation's auth user id and published: false
After the insert it navigates to previewEvent with the new row; only previewEvent's handlePublish (update published: true by id) publishes it
Students only receive it through fetchAllEvents, which selects published = true events whose campus equals the student's chosen campus

questions.q: If I rename or change a value in the shared categories list, what else is affected?
facts: categories (app/individual/index/data/categories.ts) is imported by registerIndividual, registerOrg, the student EditProfileDrawer, the org categorydrawer and multiselect, and both search screens
Its value strings are persisted: individual.interests at student sign-up, organizations.type at organisation sign-up, and events.type through the event category picker
YouMightLike scores by lower-cased overlap of event.type with user.interests, so a renamed value stops matching rows that already store the old string

questions.q: What calls fetchAllEvents, and what would break if I changed how it filters by campus?
facts: It is called by the student home (refreshEvents), the organisation 'other events' tab, and at the end of both registerIndividual and registerOrg
It keeps published = true events whose campus exactly equals its argument, drops events before today, and overwrites the single 'events' AsyncStorage key
The home screen passes the university's full name, which is what event creation stores in events.campus; registration passes the abbreviation 'UIUC', which matches no stored campus
The organisation tab passes user.campus from the cached organizations row

questions.q: What makes an event a 'draft', 'ongoing' or 'archived' event? Is there a status field?
facts: There is no status column; the state is derived from events.published and events.date
Draft = published false; ongoing = published true and date today or later; archive = published true and date before startOfDay(today)
Each organisation list (draft.tsx, ongoing.tsx, archive.tsx) queries only events whose uuid equals the signed-in organisation's id, then filters dates on the client
The archive-event edge function archives nothing: it is the template 'Hello {name}' handler

questions.q: How does the app tell a student account from an organisation account, and what represents each?
facts: Both are Supabase auth users; the role is implied by which table has a row whose id equals the auth user id: individual (students) or organizations. There is no role column or claim
The root layout (and login) query individual first and route to /individual, otherwise query organizations and route to /org
Student rows are created with id, email, full_name and interests; organisation rows with id, email, org_name and type (a category array)
Whichever row is found is cached under the same 'user' key, so screens read user.full_name or user.org_name from it

questions.q: How would I add a new screen to the organisation side, for example an analytics page opened from the organisation home?
facts: Routes are files (expo-router): add app/org/index/<name>.tsx; app/org/index/_layout.tsx is a header-less Stack that picks up new files without listing them
Open it by file name with navigation.navigate('<name>', params), as the organisation home does for 'addEvent'
A new bottom tab instead needs a folder with its own _layout.tsx plus a Tabs.Screen entry in app/org/_layout.tsx (otherevents, index, account)
Detail screens hide the tab bar themselves with navigation.getParent()?.setOptions({ tabBarStyle: { display: 'none' } })

questions.q: Where would I add a new event field, say a capacity limit, so organisations can set it and students can see it?
facts: The repo has no database schema or migrations (supabase/ holds config.toml, an empty seed.sql and the functions), so the column must be added in the hosted Supabase project
The field has to be added to both the insert payload in addEvent.tsx and the update in editEvent/[id].tsx, which are separate copies of the event form
There is no shared Event type: about twenty screens each declare their own local Event interface, so each display screen is updated one by one
Student reads use select('*') in fetchAllEvents, so a new column reaches the cached 'events' list without changing the query

questions.q: Who is allowed to edit, publish or delete an event, and where is that checked?
facts: On the client, the only ownership filter is that the organisation lists load events whose uuid equals the signed-in organisation's id
Edit (editEvent updateEvent), publish (previewEvent handlePublish) and delete (handleDeleteEvent in draft/ongoing/archive) all filter by event id only, with no uuid condition
The repo contains no SQL schema or row-level-security policies, so any server-side restriction exists only in the hosted Supabase project; the client uses the public anon key
Student clients must also be able to update events rows: RSVP and cancel rewrite events.rsvp directly by event id

questions.q: Is account deletion protected so a user can only delete their own account, and does it work for both account types?
facts: delete-user takes the Authorization bearer token, resolves the user with auth.getUser(token) and returns 401 when there is no valid user
The { userId } the client sends in the body is ignored; the id comes only from the token
With the service-role key it deletes the individual row and then the auth user; it never touches organizations or events, so the student's entries in events.rsvp remain
The organisation account screen invokes 'delete-organization', a function that does not exist in supabase/functions

questions.q: Where is the password rule enforced, and is it enforced on every path that sets a password?
facts: The rule (at least 8 characters, one capital, one digit) is the isPasswordValid regex, duplicated in registerIndividual and registerOrg
It only disables the stage-4 Continue button; supabase.auth.signUp was already called earlier with a generated temporary password just to send the email code
resetPassword only checks that the code and new password are non-empty before calling auth.updateUser; no strength rule applies
For organisation accounts, the reset also writes the new password in plain text to organizations.password
